literal: Eye possessors those-who-are-called learned-ones; on-face two sore possessors unlearned-ones.
translation: The learned are the only ones who can truly be said to possess eyes. The unlearned merely have two sores on their face.
modern: கண் உடையவர்கள் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவர்கள் கற்றவர்கள் மட்டுமே. கல்வி கற்காதவர்கள் முகத்தில் உள்ளவை கண்கள் அல்ல, அவை இரண்டு புண்கள் ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the educated and the uneducated by redefining what it means to have sight. It declares that only learned people truly possess eyes, as education grants them the inner vision to perceive and understand reality. For those who remain unlearned, their physical eyes are completely useless. The poet uses the striking word 'புண்' (sore or wound) to describe the eyes of the uneducated, suggesting that without the light of knowledge, these organs are merely blind blemishes on the face.
